facts.statement: The type specimen of Jianchangosaurus was a juvenile discovered in Jianchang County, western Liaoning Province.
facts.quote: The type specimen, a juvenile, was discovered in Jianchang County, in the western part of Liaoning Province.

facts.statement: Despite being a basal therizinosaur, Jianchangosaurus possessed key anatomical features like a beaked premaxilla and a specific pubic boot shape.
facts.quote: In spite of its basal position, Jianchangosaurus already bore many of the hallmarks of therizinosaur anatomy, such as a beaked premaxilla, and the shape of the pubic boot.

facts.statement: The genus name Jianchangosaurus is derived from the discovery county and the Greek word for lizard.
facts.quote: The genus name is derived from the county where the specimen was found, and the Greek word "sauros" (σαυρος), meaning "lizard".

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated the holotype's weight at around 20 kg but expressed uncertainty about its total length due to the missing tail tip.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul estimated the weight of the holotype specimen around 20 kg, though expressed uncertainty about its total body length, due to the fact that tail tip is unpreserved.

facts.statement: In 2024, Gregory S. Paul suggested a revised body mass estimate of 26 kg for the holotype.
facts.quote: In 2024, he suggested a higher body mass of 26 kg

facts.statement: The premaxilla and the front portion of the maxilla in Jianchangosaurus lacked teeth.
facts.quote: The premaxilla and the anterior (front) portion of the maxilla are edentulous, meaning they lacked teeth.

facts.statement: Small foramina on the premaxilla suggest that Jianchangosaurus had a beak.
facts.quote: The premaxilla is lined with small foramina, suggesting that a beak was present.

facts.statement: Jianchangosaurus had small, lance-shaped teeth that consistently featured three denticles of equal size.
facts.quote: The teeth were small and lanceolate (shaped like the tip of a lance). The teeth consistently have three denticles of equal size.

facts.statement: Jianchangosaurus's dental morphology likely maximized biting stress to help it effectively slice plant fibers.
facts.quote: A similar dental morphology is seen in ornithopods and ceratopsians, and likely maximised biting stress during occlusion, allowing Jianchangosaurus to more effectively slice plant fibres.

facts.statement: The preserved skeleton of Jianchangosaurus includes ten cervical vertebrae ranging from the atlas to the last neck bone.
facts.quote: Ten cervical (neck) vertebrae are preserved in Jianchangosaurus, consisting of the atlas (first cervical vertebra), axis (second cervical vertebra), and all of the following vertebrae.

facts.statement: All preserved neck vertebrae of Jianchangosaurus are amphicoelous (concave at both ends) and highly pneumatized.
facts.quote: All of the preserved cervical vertebrae are amphicoelous, meaning that they were concave at both ends, and were also highly pneumatised.

facts.statement: Jianchangosaurus possessed at least sixteen spint-shaped gastralia that supported abdominal organs and provided muscle attachment sites.
facts.quote: At least sixteen gastralia, bones which would have supported the abdominal organs and served as muscle attachment sites, were present. They were spint-like in shape.

facts.statement: The scapula and coracoid bones were unfused in Jianchangosaurus, a condition seen in other basal therizinosaurs but possibly due to its juvenile status.
facts.quote: The scapula and coracoid of Jianchangosaurus were unfused, like in other basal therizinosaurs, though this may be due to its nature as a juvenile.

facts.statement: The humerus of Jianchangosaurus measured 158.5 mm in length, which is slightly shorter than the scapula.
facts.quote: The humerus measured 158.5 mm in length, slightly shorter than the scapula.

facts.statement: Four distal carpals were preserved, including the semilunate carpal, a characteristic feature of maniraptorans.
facts.quote: Four distal carpals are preserved, including the semilunate carpal that characterises maniraptorans.

facts.statement: The hand claws of Jianchangosaurus were curved and narrow in transverse section.
facts.quote: The manual unguals (hand claws) were curved, and were narrow transversely.

facts.statement: Four foot claws were known, all recurved and transversely compressed with poorly developed flexor tubercles, similar to those in Erlikosaurus.
facts.quote: Four pedal unguals are known, all with poorly developed flexor tubercules. All of them are recurved and transversely compressed, similar to in Erlikosaurus.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Jianchangosaurus is an almost complete skeleton of a single juvenile individual, lacking only the distal part of the tail.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo de Jianchangosaurus 41HIII-0308A es un esqueleto casi completo de un único individuo juvenil, que solo carece de la parte distal de la cola.

facts.statement: Jianchangosaurus is estimated to have stood one meter high at the hips and measured approximately two meters in length.
facts.quote: Se estima que Jianchangosaurus medía un metro de altura hasta las caderas y aproximadamente 2 metros de largo.

facts.statement: The tibia, measuring 316 mm, was 1.5 times longer than the 206 mm femur, representing the highest known ratio in therizinosaurs and correlating strongly with cursorial habits.
facts.quote: La tibia, de 316 milímetros, es 1,5 veces más larga que el fémur, 206 milímetros, la cual es la más alta proporción conocida en tericinosaurios, una adaptación que está fuertemente correlacionada con el desarrollo de los hábitos cursoriales en los dinosaurios.

facts.statement: Wide and unbranched feather impressions surround the holotype of Jianchangosaurus, with only their distal ends visible.
facts.quote: The impressions of a series of wide and unbranched feathers surround the holotype of Jianchangosaurus. Only their distal ends are visible.

facts.statement: Researchers speculated that the wide and unbranched feathers of Jianchangosaurus may have been used for visual display.
facts.quote: The describers of Jianchangosaurus speculated that they may have been used for visual display.

facts.statement: Jianchangosaurus lived during the early Cretaceous period, approximately 126 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a principios del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 126 millones de años, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: Jianchangosaurus is classified as a basal therizinosaur, similar to the primitive genera Falcarius and Beipiaosaurus.
facts.quote: Like the primitive Falcarius and Beipiaosaurus, Jianchangosaurus was classified as a basal therizinosaur.

facts.statement: Jianchangosaurus is the only known therizinosaur with tail vertebrae (caudal centra) that are oval in shape.
facts.quote: Jianchangosaurus is the only known therizinosaur that possesses a tail with caudal centra that are oval in shape.

facts.statement: The validity of Jianchangosaurus is debated, with Cau (2024) arguing it is a junior synonym of Beipiaosaurus because distinguishing features are based on ontogenetically variable characters.
facts.quote: The validity of Jianchangosaurus was called into question by Cau (2024), who considered it to be a junior synonym of the contemporary Beipiaosaurus since the diagnosis distinguishing the taxa was based on ontogenetically variable characters.

facts.statement: Liao and colleagues (2026) supported the distinction of Jianchangosaurus from Beipiaosaurus, suggesting the former was better adapted for running while the latter had a more robust, less cursorial morphology.
facts.quote: In their 2026 description of the contemporary Kayrasaurus, Liao and colleagues supported the validity and distinction of all four Yixian therizinosaurs, with Jianchangosaurus and Lingyuanosaurus being better adapted to running, and Beipiaosaurus and Kayrasaurus having a less cursorial and more robust morphology.

facts.statement: The skull of Jianchangosaurus measures 230 millimeters in length and is 10% longer than the femur.
facts.quote: El cráneo mide 230 milímetros de longitud y es un 10% más largo que el fémur

facts.statement: Jianchangosaurus possesses 27 maxillary teeth and approximately 25 to 25 dentary teeth.
facts.quote: Jianchangosaurus posee 27 dientes maxilares y aproximadamente 25 a 28 dientes dentarios

facts.statement: Researchers hypothesized that the short toothless region of the upper jaw was covered by a rhamphotheca, similar to modern birds.
facts.quote: Los investigadores observaron, que, en la parte frontal de la mandíbula superior, el premaxilar es desdentada, cuando se compara con la larga región desdentada de Erlikosaurus andrewsi, la de Jianchangosaurus yixianensis es relativamente corto y plantearon la hipótesis de que estaba cubierta por un rhamphotheca

facts.statement: The lower jaw was rotated downward to work with the upper rhamphotheca for stripping food.
facts.quote: La parte frontal de la mandíbula inferior está girada hacia abajo y, en combinación con la rhamphotheca de la mandíbula superior, funciona para arrancar la comida

facts.statement: Derived skull features suggest adaptations for feeding on plant material.
facts.quote: Las características derivadas presentes en el cráneo de este género sugieren adaptaciones para alimentarse de material vegetal

facts.statement: In 2013, Pu et al. noted that the dental morphology likely maximized bite stress to cut plant fibers, similar to ornithopods and ceratopsians.
facts.quote: Pu et al. en 2013, notaron que esta morfología dental "probablemente maximiza el estrés de mordedura durante la oclusión para cortar fibras de material vegetal, similar a ornitópodos y ceratopsianos"

facts.statement: The crowns of Jianchangosaurus teeth decrease in size as they progress toward the back of the skull.
facts.quote: Las coronas de sus dientes disminuyen de tamaño a medida que avanzan hacia la parte posterior del cráneo

facts.statement: The teeth in the lower jaw have inverted morphology where the outer surface is concave.
facts.quote: Los dientes en la mandíbula inferior poseen la morfología invertida, donde la superficie del diente que mira hacia el exterior es cóncava

facts.statement: Fossil impressions revealed a series of wide, unbranched feathers.
facts.quote: Las impresiones de una serie de plumas anchas y no ramificadas fueron descubiertas con los fósiles

facts.statement: Based on their morphology, the feathers are considered primitive and resemble those found on the neck of Beipiaosaurus.
facts.quote: Sobre la base de su morfología, las plumas se consideran primitivas y se asemejan a las que se encuentran a lo largo del cuello de Beipiaosaurus

facts.statement: The presence of wide, elongated filamentous feathers suggests they may have been used for display.
facts.quote: Los autores señalaron que la "presencia de plumas filamentosas anchas alargadas (EBFF) sugiere que podrían haberse utilizado para la visualización"

facts.statement: The only known skeleton of Jianchangosaurus belongs to a juvenile individual.
facts.quote: El único esqueleto de Jianchangosaurus conocido es el de un individuo juvenil

facts.statement: The unfused scapula and coracoid suggest the specimen is a juvenile, though this condition is also seen in some adult basal therizinosaurids.
facts.quote: La escápula y el coracoide tampoco están fusionados, lo que, según los autores, puede ser una característica ontogenética en Jianchangosaurus, lo que también sugiere que es un juvenil

facts.statement: Jianchangosaurus possessed barely curved hand claws with weak flexor tubercles positioned ventrally relative to the articular face.
facts.quote: La presencia de unguales de la mano apenas curvados con tubérculos flexores débiles posicionados ventralmente con respecto a la cara articular

facts.statement: The ilium of Jianchangosaurus is shallow and elongated.
facts.quote: El ilion es poco profundo y alargado

facts.statement: Fossil remains, an almost complete juvenile specimen missing the distal tail, were found in the Yixian Formation in Liaoning, northeast China.
facts.quote: Sus restos fósiles, un espécimen juvenil casi completo, le falta de la parte distal de la cola, han aparecido en la Formación Yixian en Liaoning, noreste de China

facts.statement: Jianchangosaurus is estimated to have been two meters long and one meter high at the hip.
facts.quote: Se calcula que medía dos metros de largo y tenía un metro de altura en la cadera

facts.statement: Jianchangosaurus was described and named by Hanyong Pu, Yoshitsugu Kobayashi, Junchang Lu, Li Xu, Yanhua Wu, Huali Chang, Jiming Zhang, and Songhai Jia in 2013.
facts.quote: Jianchangosaurus fue descrito y nombrado por Hanyong Pu, Yoshitsugu Kobayashi, Junchang Lu, Li Xu, Yanhua Wu, Huali Chang, Jiming Zhang y Songhai Jia en 2013

facts.statement: Jianchangosaurus was classified as a basal therizinosaur, similar to Falcarius utahensis and Beipiaosaurus inexpectus.
facts.quote: Como los dinosaurios Falcarius utahensis y Beipiaosaurus inexpectus, Jianchangosaurus fue clasificado como un tericinosaurio basal

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses suggest Jianchangosaurus is more derived than Falcarius but more primitive than Beipiaosaurus.
facts.quote: Los análisis filogenético sugieren que es más derivado que Falcarius pero más primitivo que Beipiaosaurus

facts.statement: Jianchangosaurus yixianensis is the only known therizinosaur with a tail featuring caudal centra that are oval in shape.
facts.quote: Jianchangosaurus yixianensis es el único tericinosaurio conocido que posee una cola con centros caudales que tienen una forma oval

facts.statement: Jianchangosaurus lived during the Barremian to Aptian stages, between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 119.57 million years ago)
